properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's question, 2026-08-16: "we used to have a planned capabilities increment / planned epochs within reflow2 — can we use these features within reflow2 to map out the triage fixes?" The reconnaissance and the options are mine.

THE SHORT ANSWER IS YES, THE MACHINERY EXISTS AND WORKS. Measured today: `plan_epoch` (future) is distinct from `add_epoch` (happened); `schedule_for` carries `modality: expected | required` with real teeth; `arrival_delta` computes five outcomes and stores none; 11 planned epochs and 27 SCHEDULED_FOR edges already exist. `arrival_delta` on `epoch:governance-becomes-expressible` returned six outstanding requirements AND volunteered "nothing is scheduled `required` … so there is no obligation to miss and it is NOT ready to cut. An increment that promises nothing has not been scoped." The tools are healthy and opinionated.

⭐ BUT THERE IS A BLOCKER THE QUESTION DOES NOT ANTICIPATE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DECISION: `schedule_for` accepts `Requirement` or `Capability` ONLY. EVERY triage finding is a TemporalFact. So not one of them can be scheduled as it stands. The plan-increments skill says why this is correct rather than a limitation — "a plan is not intent … an item scheduled but never captured is a promise with no requirement behind it" — so the missing step is CAPTURE, not scheduling.

📌 AND THE SKILL ALREADY NAMED WHAT I WAS DOING: "if you are maintaining a numbered list of upcoming work in the conversation … that is a delivery plan living outside the graph." My ranked what-next list was exactly that, twice today, and it would have died with the session.

⚠️ EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS WORTH DOING PROPERLY RATHER THAN QUICKLY — reflow2's OWN plan has drifted, in precisely the shape the skill's §4 warns about. Of 27 SCHEDULED_FOR edges, ELEVEN still point at `rel:v0190`, `rel:v0200` and `rel:v0210`, all long shipped. Planned epochs sit at sequence 250–267 while arrived epochs reach 343. So the plan looks present and is answering nobody. Any new plan laid on top inherits that unless the stale half is dealt with.

THE OPTIONS FOR WHAT BECOMES PLANNABLE.

(a) A CAPABILITY PER FIX, at `status: planned`. Faithful to how features are tracked. ⇒ AGAINST: most of these are repair, not new function — "propose_heal stops mislabelling its scope" is restoring intended behaviour, and filing it as a capability inflates the capability count with maintenance and makes `unrealized_capability` noisier for months.

(b) A REQUIREMENT PER FIX, capabilities beneath where one is genuinely new. Faithful to the vocabulary: a fix is a statement about what must be true. ⇒ AGAINST: roughly a dozen findings would become a dozen requirements, which is a lot of intent minted in one act, and some are small enough that a requirement overstates them.

(c) ⭐ A REQUIREMENT PER THEME, several findings beneath each — and today's findings cluster harder than they look. At least four are ONE statement: "a report says whether a check was EXERCISED or had NOTHING TO EXAMINE." That covers propose_heal's vacuous zero, and it is not new doctrine — `chg:a-null-and-a-vacuous-zero-now-say-which-they-are` already did exactly this for scoped `detect_gaps`, and dev_storyflow named it a WIN. A second theme is "a reply says what it did not recognise", covering the undeclared property and the nearest-name suggestion. ⇒ AGAINST: theming is a judgement, and grouping wrongly buries a finding under a heading nobody searches.

(d) SCHEDULE NOTHING; leave them as facts and let the loop surface them. ⇒ AGAINST, and this is measured rather than argued: across this entire session `loop_status` reported the same 80 gaps and 16 defects and NEVER ONCE surfaced a triage item, because a defect FACT is not a gap. Doing nothing means they stay invisible to the loop that exists to say what is owed.

(e) EXTEND `schedule_for` TO ACCEPT A TemporalFact. Removes the blocker directly. ⇒ AGAINST: a fact is an observation, not work. Scheduling an observation is a category error, and it would let the design promise to deliver a measurement.

AND THE SECOND QUESTION, WHICH IS SEPARABLE: HOW MANY EPOCHS? One "triage fixes" epoch is easy to reason about and hard to argue with; two or three themed epochs (the detectors that misdescribe themselves, the write surface that accepts what it should question, the loop that cannot scope itself) carry more meaning and cost more to keep honest. `arrival_delta`'s own note argues for at least one `required` item per epoch, or it is not scoped.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the stale SCHEDULED_FOR edges to shipped releases should be cleaned first, retired deliberately, or left as the historical record they arguably are — that is its own decision and re-pointing them silently would erase the slip, which the tool explicitly warns against.
properties.name: OPEN — the triage findings are TemporalFacts and schedule_for takes only a Requirement or Capability, so nothing today can be planned. What becomes the plannable thing, and how many of them are there?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's idea; the blocker, the drift measurement and the five options are mine. Recorded rather than acted on because the choice mints intent.

⭐ SETTLED 2026-08-16 ON HIS WORD: "one triage fixes epoch, requirement per theme." That is option (c) for the plannable unit and ONE epoch for the container.

WHAT THAT RULES OUT, recorded because the roads not taken are the useful half: (a) a Capability per fix is declined — most of these are repair rather than new function and would inflate the capability count with maintenance; (b) a Requirement per fix is declined — roughly a dozen at once is too much intent minted in one act; (d) leaving them as facts is declined, and the measurement is why: `loop_status` reported the same 80 gaps and 16 defects all session and never once surfaced a triage item, because a defect FACT is not a gap; (e) extending `schedule_for` to accept a TemporalFact is declined as a category error — a fact is an observation, not work.

AND HE CHOSE ONE EPOCH over two or three themed ones — easier to reason about and harder to argue with, at the cost of the increment carrying less meaning in its name.

⚠️ WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT DECIDE, and was not asked: nothing is scheduled `required`. Every item goes in `expected`, because `required` is an obligation whose miss is a computed violation rather than a slip, and the plan-increments skill says to ask rather than assume. ⇒ `arrival_delta` will therefore report this epoch NOT ready to cut until somebody names at least one obligation. That is the tool being right, not a defect, and it is the next question for him.

AND THE STALE HALF IS STILL OPEN: eleven SCHEDULED_FOR edges still point at releases shipped long ago. This ruling adds a new plan beside them and does not clean them, deliberately — re-pointing them silently would erase the slip.
